> Every number below was read off the hosted `sig-pg` spine (Cloud SQL, `db-custom-2-8192`, per ADR-102) on
> 2026-09-24, or taken from the JSON summary each Cloud Run execution printed. Nothing is projected or
> estimated. Counts are counts, never population totals (§32 / SIG-METRIC-008). The resolution eval stays
> **PROVISIONAL** (D-R6.1-EVAL's first-principles half is still OPEN).

| step | what | where |
|---|---|---|

The write path is latency-bound (P30.1), so every materializer ran as a Cloud Run execution next to the
database — not over a WAN proxy. Each pass read the whole spine (1,955,004 `(subject, predicate)` groups over
2,280,784 tier-0 claims) in a few minutes; the dominant cost was the read + in-process resolve, not writes.

## 4. Deviation — coverage negative space measured, not materialized (ADR-103, D-P30.2-1)

On the hosted spine every entity with claims is typed `deployment` (246,993 subjects), so the P28.4
peer-class rule treats the whole spine as one class that tracks all 116 predicates any subject carries. The
negative space it would write is **26,696,184** `not_researched` rows (246,993 × 116 − 1,955,004 claimed
pairs; measured with one read-only query) — about 12× the spine, and almost all of it meaningless (a
traffic camera "not researched" for `bill_title` or `amount`). The metrics were materialized; the negative
space is carried by **D-P30.2-1** (a peer-class refinement — e.g. by source/connector class — before it is
materialized).

## 5. Finding fixed in this ticket — COVERAGE-RESOLVED-01

The first coverage pass wrote `subjects with a resolved claimed_device_count value` = **1 of 1**: the P28.4
ratio counted the OKC `unresolved_conflict` envelope (no winning claim) as a resolved value — publishing a
kept-open contradiction as resolved (§3.1). Fixed: the numerator counts only decisions with a
`winning_claim`, and `read_materialized_coverage` returns the latest append-only measurement per quantity.
The re-run appended the corrected 0-of-1 row (+1, the other 116 +0); the 1-of-1 row stays in the table as
history and is no longer surfaced. Both are test-pinned over real PG18+PostGIS
(`tests/db/test_coverage_materialize.py`).

## 6. Hosted-scale resolution eval (D-R6.1-EVAL, hosted half)

| measure | value |
|---|---|
| observation-level sites (tier-0 subjects with a `camera_latitude`/`camera_longitude` claim) | **230,267** |
| resolved sites (those sites with a materialized decision that picked a winning claim) | **0** |
| resolution envelopes materialized | **8** (7 resolved, 1 unresolved_conflict) |
| dedup ratio (resolved sites / observation sites) | **0.000**; entity-level merges (`entity.merged_into`) = **0** |
| auto-write demotions at the 0.98 floor | **0** (tier-0 holdout precision 1.000 — the PROVISIONAL bootstrap eval) |

Why 0 resolved sites: 1,954,996 of the 1,955,004 groups use predicates with no row in the resolver's predicate
registry — the camera-registry predicates (`camera_latitude`, `camera_longitude`, `camera_operator`,
`camera_external_ref`, `external_id`, …) that make up almost the whole spine. With no registry row, no claim
in those groups is admissible and nothing is adjudicated (SIG-RECON-013). The write path works (8 envelopes,
+0 on re-run); the gap is registry coverage, carried by **D-P30.2-3**. Until it closes, the P28.5 surface
shows the observation-level framing — no fabricated resolved-site count. Refreshed in
`P28.1_resolution_eval.md` (committed data: `p30.2-hosted/resolution_scale.json`).

## 7. Observations (recorded, not changed here)

- **Detector mapping granularity.** §33.2 maps a plain `value_disagreement` to `conflicting_retention`
  (documented as a deliberate many-to-one in `tasks/catalog.py`), so the OKC device-count conflict is queued
  with a retention-worded closing condition and a surveillance-policy records template. The spec's catalog
  sets this; changing it needs its own decision.
- **ENTITY-RACE-01** (the duplicate `camreg_camilo_schools` entity from P30.1) did not surface: no resolution
  or merge touched it.
